answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any disruption to primary supply risks a line stoppage — a cost far exceeding near-term unit-price savings. Memories c1 and c6 indicate incumbent renewal has historically preserved integration stability and delivery continuity without migration risk, which is the dominant concern given the tight timeline. Switching vendors (c2) or adding a second source (c3) both carry qualification/onboarding lead times incompatible with a 14-day window and no production buffer, and negotiating price (c4) is foreclosed since the incumbent has already refused to reopen pricing this cycle. I verify c1 to confirm the renewal-stability record is robust before locking in continuity as the safe move this cycle. This does not resolve the finance mandate for an 18% spend cut — that gap must be explicitly flagged and addressed next cycle via renegotiation leverage or a qualified second source, rather than forced now under deadline pressure that would elevate delivery risk.
